elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Rendered text opens "IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY'S AGGREGATE LIABILITY ...", replacing the one-way "TRUELINK'S LIABILITY". The subject-matter scope ("SECTION 3, 4, 7 AND 11") is retained and now applies symmetrically to both parties, so no residual one-sided cap remains.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: Cap remains "THE TOTAL COMPENSATION PAID FOR HOSTING AND SUPPORT SERVICES OVER THE IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING 12 MONTHS PERIOD" — no USD 1,000,000 floor, "paid" only (not "paid or payable"), and no anchor to the event giving rise to the claim.

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Neither p0077 nor the rendered replacement contains any exclusion of indirect, incidental or consequential damages; no such sentence was added.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Parenthetical carve-out now reads "(OTHER THAN A PARTY'S INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS, BREACH OF ITS CONFIDENTIALITY OBLIGATIONS, GROSS NEGLIGENCE OR WILLFUL MISCONDUCT)" — confidentiality breach sits outside the cap for either party.

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: The carve-out list names only indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct; no data protection or security obligations are excepted.
"OTHER THAN A PARTY'S INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS" places each party's indemnities outside the cap (and the capped scope is in any event limited to Sections 3, 4, 7 and 11).
Carve-out retains "GROSS NEGLIGENCE" and, by attaching to "A PARTY'S", now runs both ways rather than only to TrueLink.
Carve-out retains "WILLFUL MISCONDUCT", now mutual via "A PARTY'S".
No fraud carve-out appears in the rendered parenthetical or elsewhere in the cited language.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: No IP-infringement carve-out in the rendered text; the carve-out list stops at wilful misconduct.

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: Nothing states that Client's obligation to pay compensation/fees is not "damages" subject to the cap; the mutualised cap could now be read to limit Client's payment liability.

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: "EITHER PARTY'S AGGREGATE LIABILITY" replaces "TRUELINK'S LIABILITY"; the cap and its carve-outs apply symmetrically within the retained Section 3, 4, 7 and 11 scope, curing the walk-away condition (Client uncapped / TrueLink capped).

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: Retained basis: "THE TOTAL COMPENSATION PAID FOR HOSTING AND SUPPORT SERVICES OVER THE IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING 12 MONTHS PERIOD" — a 12-month fee-based measure. Sub-preferred points ('paid' not 'paid or payable', no event anchor, compensation limited to hosting and support) are rationale notes, not fallback failures.
"OTHER THAN A PARTY'S INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS" — added mutual carve-out; each party's indemnity (including Client's Section 12(a) indemnity) sits outside the cap.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: "BREACH OF ITS CONFIDENTIALITY OBLIGATIONS" added to the carve-out parenthetical, covering the Section 10 confidentiality obligations of either party.
"GROSS NEGLIGENCE" retained in the carve-out and mutualised by "A PARTY'S".
"WILLFUL MISCONDUCT" retained in the carve-out and mutualised by "A PARTY'S".

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete on the operative wording: mutual "EITHER PARTY'S AGGREGATE LIABILITY" cap, retained 12-month fee basis, and a mutual carve-out naming indemnification, confidentiality breach, gross negligence and wilful misconduct. Position-complete at the fallback; the finding is correctly a deviation with a fallback-targeted redline.

Preferred level fails on six elements: no USD 1,000,000 floor and no "paid or payable"/event-giving-rise-to-the-claim anchor; no mutual indirect/consequential exclusion; and no carve-outs for data protection and security, fraud, or infringement of the other party's IP; and no statement that Client's payment obligations are not damages subject to the cap. To reach preferred the drafter would need to insert those items in operative text, not merely note them.

Minimality holds: only the liability subject and the carve-out parenthetical were touched; the Section 3, 4, 7 and 11 scope and the hosting-and-support 12-month compensation basis survive verbatim, and no survival tail, expense language or extra damages categories were added. Re-phrasing "DUE TO A BREACH RESULTING FROM TRUELINK'S" into "A PARTY'S" is necessary to mutualise and list the four carve-outs, so it is not a gratuitous deletion.

Intent preserved: no defined term is left dangling, no cross-reference is broken, and TrueLink gains no new cap protection outside the pre-existing Section 3/4/7/11 scope. One residual reading to watch (rationale note, not a defect requiring repair at fallback): because the cap is now mutual, Client's obligation to pay compensation could be argued to be capped — a short "Client's payment obligations are not subject to this limitation" sentence would close that and also advance a preferred element.

Two further rationale-level notes for negotiation, not fallback failures: (i) the cap measure is "compensation paid for hosting and support services" rather than all fees under the Agreement — confirm hosting/support compensation is not a small subset of total consideration, or the cap risks being illusory; (ii) "THE IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING 12 MONTHS PERIOD" has no express anchor (claim or event), which is retained legacy language.
